datasheet.title: EX4400 Line of Ethernet Switches Datasheet (Juniper Networks, French-language PDF created 2025-10-14)

description: Juniper EX4400-24X campus and distribution switch, 1RU. It has 24 SFP/SFP+ ports that take 1GbE or 10GbE optics, in 12 columns of two cages. The front also holds two 100GbE QSFP28 ports and the console, management and USB-A ports. It has a USB-C console port, the chassis and port mode lamps, a mode button and one extension module slot. The rear holds two fan modules and two power supply slots. A shipped switch carries one 550 W supply, two fan modules and covers on the empty slots. The configurations give the supply type and the airflow.

status-leds.description: the chassis status and port mode lamps at the right of the front panel

name: ex4400-24x

airflow.note: Tables 14 and 16 - the 24X is sold front-to-back (AIR OUT label, orange handle) as EX4400-24X and EX4400-24X-DC, and back-to-front (AIR IN label, blue handle) as EX4400-24X-AFI and EX4400-24X-DC-AFI. The handle colour of each fan module and supply follows the guide.

colour.note: Median of bare face on the guide renders (#777777) and of the status plate (#50575f), and of the ground plate on the rear render (#aab4b7, silver here where the other EX4400 rears draw it dark). The studio photograph shows the same mid-grey finish. The legends of the non-PoE models are near white on the render.

extension-slot.note: Figure 16 callout 8. The slot is a recess 363.8 to 437.8 across and 17.7 to 41.2 down in the render of Figure 14, the same place as on the other EX4400 faces. The slot is a bay. It takes the three extension modules the guide names and ships with a cover, because the shipped-components statement under Table 15 names one cover for the empty extension module slot.

gate-1.note: Figure 14 (g022907, 1500 x 199 px, embedded image extracted from the PDF) gives a face 1297 px wide (83 to 1379.5) and about 127 px tall, which is 2.936 px per mm across on the stated 441.7 mm and 2.92 down on 43.7 mm, 0.5 percent apart. The SFP cage width, measured on a quantity the scale never saw, is 13.96 mm against the registry's 14.25 pitch less its wall. The studio photograph (1500 x 236, the face 1434 px wide, 3.25 px per mm) puts the first column at 62.8 mm and the QSFP28 block at 317.0 mm, against 63.4 and 316.7 from Figure 14. Positions are taken per axis on those scales and each reads to about half a millimetre.

grounding.note: Connect Earth Ground to an EX4400 Switch - a 2-hole protective grounding terminal on the rear panel, used with 10-32 x 0.25 in screws and the lugs LCD10-10AF-L, LCD8-10AF-L or LCD6-10AF-L. The guide gives no hole spacing. The 15.0 mm spacing is measured on the render and is estimated. The render shows two bare holes, so they are drawn as dark holes on the plate.

interface-names.note: Table 114 - the CLI addresses the switch as FPC 0, the built-in ports as PIC 0 ports 0 to 23, the two QSFP28 ports as PIC 1 ports 0 and 1, and the extension module as PIC 2. The names are not printed on the metal, so no interfaces block is written.

mgmt-ports.note: Figure 14 and Figure 16 callouts 1, 2, 10 and 11 - on this model the console (CON), management (MGMT), USB-A and reset pinhole are on the front, left of the cages. CON centre 14.3, 29.6; MGMT 33.3, 29.6; USB-A 47.4, 28.1, vertical; RESET pinhole 56.9, 33.9, with the legends under them. Figure 49 draws the two management lamps, link activity and status, as on the other models. All read off the render and estimated to half a millimetre.

mounting.note: Mounting Options and the mounting procedures - the two-post kit EX-RMK ships in the box and mounts the brackets flush with the front or along the middle of the side panels. The separately orderable EX-4PST-RMK mounts the switch flush with the front posts of a four-post rack or recessed inside it. EX-WMK is a wall kit. No ear distance in millimetres, no rack depth range and no bracket drawing that can be measured is in the guide, so the positions are named without a number and no kit is listed. The library holds no rail kit for them.

port-leds.note: Figure 51 (g022904) and Tables 43 and 44 - each port has a link activity lamp and a status lamp, four small triangles in the belly between the two cages. From the left they are the lower port's link lamp, the upper port's link lamp, the lower port's status lamp and the upper port's status lamp (callouts 4, 1, 3 and 2). The upper port's triangles point up and the lower port's down. They sit 2.6, 5.3, 8.95 and 11.65 mm from the column's left edge, 11.0 mm below the top of the upper cage, read off the render and estimated. The link lamp is green, steady for a link without traffic and blinking for traffic. The status lamp shows one parameter at a time, chosen with the mode button - for these ports 10 Gbps steady and 1000 Mbps blinking on SPD.

port-numbering.note: Figure 14 and the studio photograph - under each column one pair, an even number with an up arrow and the next odd number with a down arrow ("0 up 1 down" to "22 up 23 down"). Numbering starts at 0, as printed. The legend sits 28.1 mm below the upper cage's top, the arrows 5.9 and 11.0 mm from the column's left edge; both are estimated from the render. CLI names are not printed on the metal and Table 114 gives the ports as PIC 0 ports 0 to 23.

ports.note: Figure 14 and Figure 16 - 24 SFP/SFP+ ports in 12 columns of two stacked cages, numbered 0 to 23 as printed with the upper cage of a column even. Unlike the 48F, each column is its own cage pair with a column of vent holes between, so the columns sit 21.03 mm apart (63.69 to 295.64 mm over 11 steps) and the block is declared as 12 gangs of one, with the registry's 14.25 pitch and a 6.78 mm gutter. The first column's cage opens at 63.4 mm. The upper cage starts 9.9 mm down and the lower 14.9 mm below it, read off the render at the cage frames, so the belly row is 14.9 and not the registry's 15.0. Counts confirmed by Table 15 (1/10GbE ports 24) and Table 114 (PIC 0, 24 ports, 1G/10G SFP/SFP+).

power-supplies.note: Table 14 ships the 24X with a 550 W AC supply, and Table 16 gives the same for the other builds. The text under Figure 16 says the 24X takes 550 W AC or DC supplies, and that AC and DC must not be mixed. The rear render shows two supplies; the default here ships one supply and a cover on the second slot, as the text under Table 15 states. A bay cannot say that supplies of one chassis must match.

qsfp28.note: Figure 14 and Figure 16 callout 9 - two QSFP28 ports side by side in one row, numbered 0 and 1 on the face, with four lamps above each. The cage openings are 18.9 mm apart centre to centre on the render, which is the registry's 19.0 mm ganged pitch, so the pair is a ganged block of std/qsfp-ganged and not two single cages. The first opening starts at 316.7 mm and 25.9 mm down. The lamps are 2.9, 6.8, 10.7 and 14.7 mm from each cage's left edge and 22.1 mm down. Table 114 lists them as PIC 1 ports 0 and 1, and the guide says they can be Virtual Chassis ports with the request virtual-chassis mode hgoe command. Figures 57 and 58 and Table 46 give the lamps - the leftmost is the Virtual Chassis lamp, green steady for 100 Gbps, amber for 40 Gbps.

rear.note: Figure 15 and Figure 17 (g022897, g022899) measured on the render, per axis, from the rear left edge (the chassis right side as seen from the front). The rear has no console, management, USB or QSFP28 port, because the front holds them. Ground plate 27.8 to 61.7 across and 27.6 to 39.7 down with two holes 15.0 apart; ESD socket at 101.1, 36.0. Fan module slots are at 108.2 and 206.0 across and power supply slots at 255.0 and 346.4, with the fan or power icon and its number above each slot. These are the same positions as the other EX4400 rears, and the render agrees to 0.3 mm.

rear-labels.note: Figure 17 callouts 1, 2, 6 and 9 are the serial number ID label, the CLEI code label, the power supply rating label and the claim code label. The claim code label is a QR code. They are stickers, not metal, so each is a named region and is not drawn. The serial number strip at the left edge is estimated from the callout drawing, which is a different scale from the render.

sources.note: EX4400 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, PDF created 2026-07-22 (331 pages), fetched from www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex4400/ex4400.pdf. Taken from it - Table 4 and Table 7 (the model list), Tables 14 to 16 with Figures 14 to 18 (EX4400-24X), Table 5 (extension modules), Table 38 to Table 40 (chassis, fan and supply sizes), Tables 41 to 51 (lamps), Tables 52 to 58 (heat and supplies), Table 93 (environment), Table 114 (CLI names) and Table 115 (acoustics). Figures 14 and 15 (g022907, g022897) are renders of the real product and are the pictures measured here. Figures 16 and 17 (g022898, g022899) are the flat callout drawings, used for the callout list and the label regions. Juniper's image library, www.juniper.net/content/dam/www/assets/images/us/en/image-library/ex-series/ex4400-24x/ex4400-24x-front-high.jpg (a JPEG, 1500 x 236), is a studio view of the same face. The same pattern for the 48F, 24MP and 48MP returned an HTML 404 page, and no rear photograph exists for any of the four. The EX4400 datasheet on juniper.net (a French-language PDF of 2025-10-14, the only one the site answers for) names the 24X as 24 SFP+ 10GbE ports and lists the ten base models; no figure here comes from it. Terms - Juniper's documentation pages state no licence for the guide, so the facts are transcribed and nothing is copied; no drawing or photograph is in the repository. The held intake folder was not readable by this account, so no earlier photograph, stencil or 3D model could be used. An end-of-life search made 2026-10-20 found no notice for the EX4400 line, so the lifecycle is none-announced.

spare.note: The weight list under Table 15 prints EX4400-24X-S at 5.52 kg, but Tables 14 and 16 list no -S model and give no shipped-components or supply row for it. No -S configuration is modelled; see the gap spare-model.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md) - a belly-to-belly pair is the upper cage upright and the lower turned 180. The render shows the latch bars in the belly between the cages, which agrees. The SFP cages are stacked this way. The two QSFP28 ports are side by side in one row, so none applies to them.

status-block.note: Figure 16 callouts 4 to 7 and the studio photograph. A dark plate 361.2 to 439.5 across and 1.4 to 15.5 down, the same as the other EX4400 faces. The model name EX4400-24X is printed at the left from 367.7 to 386.1 mm, which at 3.0 mm type is 10 characters. The USB-C console port is centred at 393.7, 8.3 with the USB symbol below it. Two columns of lamps sit at 406.2 and 410.1 across - SYS, ALM, MST and CLD on the left, SPD, DX and EN on the right, with no POE lamp on a non-PoE model. The rows are at 3.8, 6.8, 9.7 and 12.8 down; the render scatters them by up to 0.5 mm and they are aligned. The mode button is a flush disc at 423.1, 8.6.

vents.note: The front has a hexagon punching in a band over and under the cage block, a column of holes beside each cage column, and a field above the QSFP28 ports. The fields are drawn as repeating patterns in simplified outlines, not hole for hole. The rear of this model has no punching.

width.note: Table 15 gives the chassis 17.39 in (44.17 cm) wide, and says the outer edges of the front mounting brackets extend the width to 19 in (48.2 cm). The face is the body between the folds, 441.7 mm, with no ears drawn. Height is 1.72 in (4.37 cm), 1RU. Depth is 15.71 in (39.9 cm) with no supply, fan module or extension module fitted, 16.93 in (43 cm) with a supply and fan modules, 17.35 in (44.07 cm) with an extension module as well. The bare figure 399.0 mm is carried as the chassis depth, because every module is its own part. The other two are in attrs.
